placement.distanceKnown: Your best distance in this session: {{everyday}}, {{dist}}.
placement.distanceDefault: A good starting point is {{everyday}} between your mouth and the mic: {{dist}}.

gain.what: is your input volume: how much the mic is turned up before anything else.
gain.where: Change it with the gain knob on your audio interface, or the mic gain slider in Wave Link.
gain.steps: Move it a little at a time, then record again to check.

beforeAfter.belowQuarter: Your effects made the room {{db}} dB quieter next to your voice — less than a quarter as loud.
beforeAfter.quarter: Your effects made the room {{db}} dB quieter next to your voice — about a quarter as loud.
beforeAfter.half: Your effects made the room {{db}} dB quieter next to your voice — about half as loud.
beforeAfter.some: Your effects made the room {{db}} dB quieter next to your voice.
beforeAfter.little: Your effects barely changed the room noise yet. The noise reduction steps in the technical details can help.
beforeAfter.floor: Your pauses are cut to digital silence, so this can't show how much room noise was really removed.

community.behind: People with this mic usually get about {{db}} dB more voice over the room noise than you do right now.
community.ahead: You get about {{db}} dB more voice over the room noise than most people with this mic.
community.same: Your voice stands out from the room about as well as most people's with this mic.

analysis.error: This take could not be analyzed
analysis.referenceNote: Reference ranges are approximate targets for close-miked spoken voice. Trust your ears over any single number.

verdict.quietBroken: Noise reading may be off: there was sound in the first 3 s.

room.title: Room noise
room.fromQuiet: Measured in the silent seconds before you read.
room.estimated: Estimated from the quietest moments of the take.
room.bars: Bars show how far your voice is above the room in each octave: under 10 dB the noise wins, 20 dB and up is clear.
room.chartAria: Voice over room noise per octave, in dB

chart.noteTone: 0 = matches a clear spoken-voice curve. Up = too much of that band, down = too little. Inside ±3 dB is fine, ±6 dB is noticeable.
chart.noteDiff: Bars up: A has more of that band than B (after level-matching). With A = processed and B = a raw control, this is what your effects change.
chart.ariaTone: Deviation from reference voice per octave

beforeAfter.title: Before / after
beforeAfter.lowered: Your effects lowered the room by {{db}} dB
beforeAfter.little: Noise reduction made little difference — check the ReaFIR profile
beforeAfter.floor: Your pauses are cut to digital silence, so this can't show how much room noise was really removed.

regressions.title: Your effects are making your voice worse
regressions.tooLoud: Your voice got too loud and hits the limit, so it distorts
regressions.quieter: Your voice got much quieter ({{db}} dB)
regressions.thin: The bass is gone, so your voice sounds thin
regressions.harsh: The upper tones got harsh and tiring
regressions.chopped: Pauses are cut to total silence, which chops your words

community.none: No community data for {{model}} yet — be the first to share.
community.rawSnrYours: Raw SNR: yours {{yours}} dB · typical {{median}} dB ({{p25}}–{{p75}})
community.chartAria: Deviation from reference voice per octave: you vs community median

settings.title: Suggested ReaPlugs settings
settings.keepMic: Keep the mic at {{dist}} and the Wave XLR gain unchanged.
settings.applyBefore: Values are a starting point: about 70% of the measured correction, so they don't overshoot. Type them into each plugin window (Wave Link → mic → Effects → the sliders icon), or close Wave Link and run
settings.applyAfter: (see tools/README.md). Record a processed take afterwards to check.
settings.whyGateNoisy: Soft expander just above the room left after noise reduction: pauses dip, words stay whole.
settings.whyGate: About 12 dB above the room noise, well under your voice.
settings.whyEq: Frequency · gain dB · bandwidth oct. Use only these bands.
settings.whyLowcut: Extra rumble on the raw mic.
settings.whyDeess: S sounds spike on the raw mic.

share.copyTitle: Mic profile, analysis numbers and suggested values for this session. No audio, device names or dates.
share.label: Share with the community
share.needMic: Set your mic model on the setup screen first
share.note: Opens a public GitHub issue with your mic profile and analysis numbers (no audio). You review it before posting.
share.truncated: The summary was too long for the link: paste it into the Summary field.

takes.title: Takes
takes.deleteConfirm: Click again to delete every take
takes.hintAB: Set A and B on any two takes to compare them.
takes.storageBlocked: This browser blocks local storage here, so takes last only until you close the tab.

refine.title: Let's fix this
refine.lead: Your effects didn't make your voice better yet. For the next try, we changed these settings:

route.reafir: Use ReaFIR to remove the room noise.
route.ai-elgato: Remove the room noise with Elgato Noise Removal (AI) instead of ReaFIR.
route.ai-nvidia: Remove the room noise with NVIDIA Broadcast (AI) instead of ReaFIR.

refine.apply: Apply the refined settings to Wave Link
refine.markedApplied: Got it. Now record again with effects so we can check these settings.
refine.byHandNote: Set these values up by hand? Tell us, so your next take with effects is checked against them.

mismatch.title: Record at the right distance first
mismatch.text: This take was recorded at {{recorded}}, but your settings were made for {{dist}}, so it can't tell whether they work. Record again at {{dist}}, or get new settings made for {{recorded}}.

approach.title: Time to try something different
approach.lead: We adjusted the settings {{n}} times and your voice still isn't better. More small changes won't fix it. These will help more:

worked.title: It worked
worked.text: With your effects your voice scores {{fx}}, up from {{raw}} without them. Save these settings as a profile to use them again.
